title: History, Ideology and Negotiation: The Politics of Policy Transition in West Bengal, India
note: Ritanjan Das’s doctoral thesis, submitted to the London School of Economics and Political Science in January 2013. Its brief historical overview describes the 1967 Naxalbari agitation, factional resistance within the CPI(M), and the announcement of CPI(ML) formation in May 1969. This is a broad political-history overview rather than a study devoted to the uprising.
whyItMatters: The thesis independently places the Naxalbari agitation within factional disputes in the CPI(M) and dates the CPI(ML) formation announcement to May 1969. Its interpretation is a short contextual overview, not a detailed account of the firing or local peasant actions.
